subject: Re: Preventing CRM logging
text: Hi Carl, lemwarm emails can indeed be logged by CRM tools like HubSpot and Salesloft. This is typically caused by the CRM's email synchronization settings, not lemwarm itself. The solution is to configure your CRM to exclude lemwarm emails using filters, labels, or specific rules within the CRM system.

subject: Re: Preventing CRM logging
text:
Hi Carl! 
 
 My colleague is currently away, I'll step in to assist you, ensuring there's no delay in addressing your needs. 🙌n them up manually. 
 
 You’re right—this is something other teams have bumped into as well, since HubSpot doesn’t allow native subject-line filtering. The workaround we usually see is to set up rules either in Gmail (before the emails get logged) or inside HubSpot with workflows. 
 
 Most teams do one of the following: 
 - Create a Gmail filter that looks for “lemwarmup” in the subject/body and either skips inbox or prevents those emails from being synced to HubSpot. Since your BDRs use the Gmail integration, this filter kicks in before HubSpot sees the email. 
- Alternatively, inside HubSpot some teams build a workflow that auto-tags or archives emails containing “lemwarmup” so they don’t clog reporting. 
 It's not a native HubSpot feature, but these small rules have worked well for others. I would also suggest double checking with CRM support as they might have a better workaround.

Hi Encrod team,

As promised we are sharing a content sample and some of the metadata tags that we care about.

We are doing this in good faith and in the interest of time. We would love to actually sign an NDA relatively soon - please feel free to share one.

Please note that when it comes to the metadata, the below is just to get the conversation going. In the end of the day, we will initially tag only what is relatively easy and cost effective, ideally right at content ingestion. We will then start adding more metadata fields to the content depending on the use case of each trining dataset we prepare.

Sample
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Pmru5SXWY7-kCjaNN6r5gBspPGs0N2VB/edit?pli=1&gid=374282107#gid=374282107￼
Beatpulse Sample Data.xlsx
docs.google.com

Initial Metadata Wishlist

Metadata Fields we need for video

Resolution (e.g., 6K, 4K, 1080p)

Frame Rate (e.g., 24fps, 30fps, 60fps)

Aspect Ratio (e.g., 16:9, 2.35:1)

Bitrate

Codec (e.g., ProRes, H.264)

Camera Model (e.g., RED Komodo 6K)

Lens Model (e.g., Canon RF 24-70mm f/2.8)

Shooting Format (e.g., RAW, LOG, compressed)

Date & Time of Capture

Audio Format (e.g., stereo, 5.1, sample rate, bit depth)

Camera Angle (e.g., high angle, low angle, eye-level, overhead)

Camera Movement (e.g., static, handheld, tracking, drone)

Shot Type (e.g., close-up, wide shot, extreme long shot)

Scene Lighting (e.g., natural light, artificial light, low light, backlit)

Depth of Field (e.g., shallow, deep)

Location Type (e.g., urban, nature, indoor, mountain, rooftop)

Weather Conditions (e.g., sunny, cloudy, foggy)

Time of Day (e.g., sunrise, midday, sunset, night)

Environment Soundscape (e.g., ambient city noise, wind, silence)

Presence of Human Subjects (yes/no)

Activity Type (e.g., rock climbing, hiking, resting)

Facial Visibility (e.g., visible, obscured, helmeted)

Primary Action/Event (e.g., climbing, preparing gear, setting anchor)

Emotion/Intensity Level (e.g., focused, relaxed, tense)

Number

subject: Re: Coordinating LVT's Encord Renewal
text:
David Hunt & Alyssa Fleming,

We have reviewed our labeling needs for products over the next 12 months.
The truth is that we do not anticipate a high demand for labeling services
over the next few months, but we do expect the demand to increase in 2026.
For this reason, we would have preferred to start with a 3,000 hour
contract, and then increase it in 2026.  As you explained in the meeting
yesterday, you can not decrease our subscription from 6,000 to 3,000 hours
without talking to your legal department.  Therefore, we would like for you
to talk to your legal department on our behalf.

Rational:

As you know, Inderjeet Singh negotiated the contract last year, and he is
no longer with LVT.  This has left us caught off-guard on some of the
details of last year's contract.  Personally, I didn't even realize it was
a subscription.  However, we do still need labeling services from Encord
for the foreseeable future.

We have just completed two contracts for labeling services of 3,000 hours
each.
- One contract was entered into on *2024-09-04* (Effective date: 2024-09-04)
- The other was entered into on *2024-10-17* (Effective date: 2024-09-04)

According to the contract, the effective date is intended to be the basis
for annual renewals.  We understand that.  However, if the effective date
of the second contract can be assigned retroactively, by 6-weeks, then we
ask as a favor, if the termination request of that contract can also be
considered, retroactively, by 6-weeks.  Please ask your legal department if
this exception can be made, and let us know.

In yesterday's meeting, we also discussed the possibility of having a
carry-over policy, where unused labeling hours from one quarter could be
consumed in the next quarter.  If possible, we would like to add such a
carry-over policy to our contact as well.

Thank you for your assistance.

--Charles Hayward
